project.title: BUS311 Individual Company Capstone
project.subtitle: CFO and Board Decision Brief
project.companyEligibility: One approved public company listed in the United States
project.audience: The selected company's CFO and Board
project.decision: One material, company-specific CFO decision, with two or three supporting actions

requirements.text: All company-specific research, evidence selection, analysis, modeling, writing, slides, the Oral Presentation, and responses to live questions are individual work.
The analysis advises the selected company's CFO and Board on one actionable company decision.

Stage 1 is exploratory: select an approved public company, learn the company basics through AI and/or ordinary web search plus required FactSet research, state one concrete FactSet learning and the screen, report, or feature used, and propose one potential CFO decision. Verification, hypothesis validation, alternatives, an evidence register, proof, and a formal approval gate are not required yet.
Explain how the company generates sales, using three to five years of consistent revenue evidence and company-specific drivers.
State one testable revenue hypothesis naming the driver, expected effect, period, and evidence that would support or falsify it.
Revenue evidence must flow into forecasts, scenarios, valuation, and the CFO decision; market valuation cannot replace the revenue analysis.
Every material figure, assumption, and claim is traceable to SEC filings, permitted FactSet evidence, Excel analysis, or another credible named source.

Beginning after Stage 1, complete exactly four bounded free-tier AI or instructor-provided equivalent checkpoints using C-A-P-A-J; independently verify retained output and record an accept, modify, or reject judgment.
Submit the working Excel model at Milestone 3 for valuation, scenarios, sensitivities, and finance-logic assessment.
Submit one editable PowerPoint company-analysis project file (.pptx) with 8-10 core slides plus an optional analytical appendix.

Deliver an individual Oral Presentation to the class on the assigned date: up to seven minutes for the decision briefing and up to three minutes for live questions, all assessed together as one Oral Presentation criterion.
A Buy/Hold/Sell rating is not required and cannot substitute for the evidence-backed CFO decision developed in later stages.

policies.individualWork: Each student owns the research, evidence selection, model, writing, slides, the Oral Presentation, and responses to live questions. Every submitted figure, formula, source choice, and recommendation must be explainable by that student.
policies.stageOneExploration: Stage 1 is a beginner-level exploration, not an evidence gate. Approved means the company fits the course scope; students do not need a separate formal approval decision before continuing. Students may use AI, ordinary web search, or both for introductory research, but FactSet use is required. They record one concrete FactSet learning and name the screen, report, or feature used without formal citation or validation at this stage.
policies.factSetAndSources: Beginning in Stage 2, material claims and model inputs must be traceable to SEC filings, permitted FactSet evidence, Excel calculations, or another credible named source. FactSet labels include item or report name, period or as-of date, units, and access date. Conflicting definitions are reconciled or disclosed.
policies.factSetPermission: Students and the instructor may use FactSet evidence in BUS311 course deliverables. Raw exports and screenshots remain in approved course-restricted systems and are not committed publicly or uploaded to public AI tools.
policies.sourceLabels: Beginning in Stage 2, for each FactSet item, name FactSet, the report/screen/chart/metric, data-through or retrieval date, units/currency/period, definition or adjustment, peer group and rationale when applicable, exact use, and limitations.
policies.verifiedAIJudgment: After Stage 1, AI may challenge student work but is never financial evidence. Retained output must be independently checked with SEC, FactSet, Excel, or course concepts and classified as accepted, modified, or rejected with a human rationale. Raw licensed data and screenshots are not uploaded to public AI tools.
policies.revenueSpine: Revenue generation, three to five years of sales evidence, company-specific drivers, a testable revenue hypothesis, and explicit forecast and decision linkage are required.
policies.milestoneDeadlines: Stages 1-4 are due at 12:30 p.m. ET (the course's class-start time) on their listed dates: Sept. 9, Sept. 30, Nov. 18, and Nov. 22, 2026.
policies.lateWork: Milestones remain eligible under the BUS311 syllabus late-work policy. A late milestone delays feedback and can make dependent project work harder; complete missing milestone work before relying on it in a later stage. Documented exceptions follow the applicable college and course process.
policies.revision: Milestones 1-3 may each be revised once within seven calendar days of written instructor feedback with a concise change log. The revised score replaces the original when higher.
policies.finalFileLock: The PowerPoint company-analysis project file is due Monday, Nov. 30, 2026 at 12:30 p.m. ET, when class begins. The submitted .pptx locks at that time for every student regardless of Oral Presentation date. Only instructor-authorized accessibility or file-repair corrections that do not alter the analysis or recommendation are permitted afterward.
policies.submissionLocation: Upload exactly one final Stage 5 file in the designated Canvas assignment: the editable PowerPoint company-analysis project (.pptx). The Oral Presentation is delivered live to the class on the assigned date and is not a second uploaded file. The Excel model is collected earlier at Milestone 3.
policies.absence: Approved documented absences use the next protected slot or instructor-scheduled make-up. The live Oral Presentation, including responses to questions, remains required. Unexcused absences follow the BUS311 late-work policy and still require a make-up Oral Presentation.

hub.purpose: Act as an internal corporate finance analyst. Diagnose how one approved public company creates revenue and value, recommend one company-specific CFO action, and defend it to the company's CFO and Board with traceable evidence and an auditable model.
hub.centralQuestion: Given the company's revenue engine, financial position, market expectations, and risks, what specific action should the CFO recommend to the Board, and what evidence makes that decision credible and implementable?

faqs.question: What is the goal of Stage 1?
faqs.answer: Explore one approved public company, learn the basics through AI and/or ordinary web search plus required FactSet research, record one concrete FactSet learning and the screen, report, or feature used, and propose one potential CFO decision.

faqs.question: Do I need to prove or validate my Stage 1 idea?
faqs.answer: No. Stage 1 is exploratory. You do not yet need to verify the recommendation, validate a hypothesis, compare or defend alternatives, build an evidence register, complete formal citations, or obtain a formal approval decision. Those tasks belong in later stages.

faqs.question: Is this a group project?
faqs.answer: No. Research, evidence selection, modeling, writing, slides, the Oral Presentation, and responses to live questions are individual work.

faqs.question: Is a Buy, Hold, or Sell recommendation enough?
faqs.answer: No. Market valuation may support the analysis, but the project requires one company-specific action the CFO could recommend to the Board.

faqs.question: Do I need a paid AI plan?
faqs.answer: No. Each checkpoint is designed for free text chat or an instructor-provided noncommercial equivalent. Browsing, uploads, connectors, image generation, and spreadsheet analysis are not required.

faqs.question: Can I upload FactSet files or screenshots to a public AI tool?
faqs.answer: No. Keep raw FactSet exports and screenshots in Canvas Course Files or another course-restricted location. Use only sanitized, student-written summaries in public AI tools.

faqs.question: Is AI output a source?
faqs.answer: No. Verify retained claims with SEC filings, permitted FactSet evidence, Excel calculations, or course concepts, then record an accept, modify, or reject judgment.

faqs.question: What happens to the Excel model at the end?
faqs.answer: The working Excel model is submitted and assessed at Milestone 3. It is not uploaded again for Stage 5, but you must be able to explain its logic and locate supporting evidence during the live Oral Presentation.

faqs.question: What do I upload and what do I present for Stage 5?
faqs.answer: Upload exactly one editable PowerPoint company-analysis project (.pptx) by the November 30 file lock. Present that submitted deck live to the class on your assigned date. The upload is worth 50 points and the live Oral Presentation is worth 25 points.

faqs.question: Which dates and submission links control if something changes?
faqs.answer: Stages 1-4 and the Stage 5 PowerPoint upload are scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET. Canvas is the authority for the live upload link, Oral Presentation order, and any later instructor-announced change.

criteria.title: Company exploration and potential CFO decision
criteria.description: Identifies an approved public company, completes introductory research, records one concrete FactSet learning, and proposes one potential company-specific CFO decision.
evidenceRules: The approved public company, ticker, exchange, and individual student are identified.
Introductory notes show AI and/or ordinary web research and clearly treat those notes as exploratory rather than verified evidence.
One specific FactSet learning is stated and the screen, report, or feature used is named; formal citation and validation are not required at Stage 1.
One potential company-specific CFO decision is proposed in the student's own words with a short explanation of why it seems worth investigating.

COMPLETE.description: The approved company and beginner-friendly snapshot are clear; one concrete FactSet learning names the feature used; and the potential CFO decision is specific, company-connected, individually authored, and appropriately tentative.

DEVELOPING.description: The submission shows a plausible start, but the company snapshot is thin, the FactSet learning or feature is vague, or the potential CFO decision is broad or weakly connected to the initial research.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED.description: The company is outside the approved course scope, required FactSet use is missing, the potential CFO decision is absent, or the work is not individually attributable.

criteria.title: Revenue engine and initial hypothesis
criteria.description: Explains how the company generates revenue, what drove three to five years of performance, and what testable hypothesis will guide the later forecast and decision.
evidenceRules: Revenue is mapped by relevant products or services, segments, geographies, customers, channels, pricing, and recurring or transactional characteristics.
Three to five years of total and material segment revenue use consistent periods, units, definitions, and traceable SEC or FactSet sources.
Company-relevant drivers are separated from temporary effects and connected to leading indicators, risks, and limitations.
The hypothesis names a driver, expected effect, period, and evidence that could support or falsify it.
A retained AI challenge is independently verified and accepted, modified, or rejected with a student rationale.

COMPLETE.description: The revenue map, reconciled multi-year evidence, company-specific drivers, indicators, risks, and a falsifiable hypothesis are complete, traceable, and connected to the later forecast and CFO decision.

DEVELOPING.description: Revenue history is partly descriptive, incompletely sourced, or weakly decomposed; the hypothesis is vague, only partly testable, or weakly challenged and verified.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED.description: Revenue generation, multi-year evidence, or the hypothesis is missing or materially inaccurate; sources or retained AI claims are unverified.

criteria.title: Valuation model and scenarios
criteria.description: Builds an auditable Excel model whose assumptions, scenarios, sensitivities, and decision outputs follow from the revenue diagnosis.
evidenceRules: Base, upside, and downside assumptions link explicitly to identified operating drivers and the developing decision.
Inputs, sources, calculations, outputs, checks, scenarios, and sensitivities are separated and labeled with units and periods.
Applicable finance logic is correct, traceable, and free of unresolved formula or sign errors.
Visible checks cover scenario consistency, valuation bridges, terminal-value reasonableness, and sensitivity links.
SEC and FactSet assumptions are labeled with item or report name and as-of date; limitations are disclosed.

COMPLETE.description: The model is revenue-linked, auditable, correctly structured, source-traceable, scenario-responsive, and free of unresolved errors; checks and sensitivities support the decision under uncertainty.

DEVELOPING.description: The model runs but has material gaps in driver linkage, sourcing, checks, scenario logic, sensitivity, or applicable finance mechanics.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED.description: The model is missing, materially incorrect, hardcoded at key outputs, disconnected from revenue evidence, or contains errors that make the valuation unreliable.

criteria.title: AI red team and revision
criteria.description: Documents bounded C-A-P-A-J challenge, independent verification, human judgment, and revision of the hypothesis, assumptions, recommendation, and Oral Presentation preparation.
evidenceRules: The record identifies context, student-written assumptions, prompt purpose, strongest challenge, and the specific output retained.
Evidence checked names the exact SEC filing, FactSet item, Excel calculation, or course concept used to test the challenge.
The student records a finding, uncertainty, accept/modify/reject judgment, and revised hypothesis or decision logic.
The final disclosure identifies tool, purpose, output retained, verification performed, and where human judgment overruled AI.
No raw licensed, private, instructor-only, or nonpublic material is supplied to a public AI tool.

COMPLETE.description: The record provides a concise verification trail showing skeptical challenge, authoritative evidence, transparent uncertainty, independent judgment, and a material revision or well-defended decision not to revise.

DEVELOPING.description: An AI interaction is recorded, but verification is shallow, the accept/modify/reject judgment is weak, or the revision and disclosure trail is incomplete.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED.description: AI output substitutes for student analysis, or verification, judgment, disclosure, privacy safeguards, or the required record is missing.

criteria.title: PowerPoint company-analysis project submission
criteria.description: Submits one editable, Board-ready PowerPoint company analysis that turns the semester's revenue, model, scenario, and red-team work into a traceable CFO recommendation and implementation plan.
evidenceRules: Exactly one editable .pptx is uploaded by the final file lock using the required filename; it contains 8-10 core slides plus an optional analytical appendix.

The requested Board decision and company-specific CFO recommendation are explicit, and three-to-five-year revenue evidence, drivers, hypothesis, and red-team revision lead into the forecast and decision.
Valuation or capital-budgeting outputs, base/upside/downside scenarios, and decision-changing sensitivities reconcile to the assessed Excel model and disclose material assumptions and limitations.
Credible alternatives are compared, and two or three supporting actions identify owners, timing, resources, dependencies, performance indicators, triggers, risks, and mitigations.
Visuals are readable, accessible, editable or traceable, and labeled with units, periods, definitions, SEC/FactSet/model source notes, and the verified AI-use disclosure.

COMPLETE.description: One on-time editable .pptx meets the slide limit and presents a precise company-specific CFO decision supported by traceable revenue evidence, a tested hypothesis, model-reconciled valuation and scenarios, credible alternatives, an actionable implementation plan, risks and limitations, accessible visuals, source notes, and verified AI disclosure.

DEVELOPING.description: An editable PowerPoint and recommendation are present, but one or more material gaps weaken decision readiness: revenue-to-valuation linkage, model reconciliation, scenarios, alternatives, implementation, risks, source notes, accessibility, traceability, file format, or slide discipline.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED.description: No usable editable .pptx is submitted, or the file is materially incomplete, generic, unsupported, inaccessible, unreconciled to the model, or does not communicate an individually authored company-analysis recommendation.

criteria.title: Oral Presentation
criteria.description: Delivers the submitted company analysis live to the class with professional Board-level communication and demonstrates individual command of the evidence, model, assumptions, alternatives, implementation, risks, and limitations.
evidenceRules: The student presents live on the assigned date using the submitted PowerPoint; the Oral Presentation is not a second uploaded file.
The decision briefing uses up to seven minutes, leads with the recommendation, explains revenue before valuation, and uses the slides as evidence rather than as a script.
Voice, pacing, transitions, terminology, and audience engagement are clear, professional, and appropriate for a CFO-and-Board audience in the classroom.

For up to three additional minutes, the student responds accurately to live questions about sources, revenue drivers, assumptions, calculations, scenarios, alternatives, implementation, risks, and conditions that would change the decision.

When uncertain, the student states the limitation and the next evidence or calculation needed; the Oral Presentation and responses demonstrate individual ownership. The briefing and question responses are scored together in this single 25-point criterion.

COMPLETE.description: The student gives a decision-led, well-paced Oral Presentation within the allotted briefing time and responds accurately and specifically to live questions, tracing sources and model logic, explaining alternatives and risks, acknowledging limits, and demonstrating clear individual ownership throughout.

DEVELOPING.description: The core message is understandable, but timing, organization, reading, jargon, pacing, audience fit, source or model command, response accuracy, treatment of alternatives and risks, or acknowledgment of uncertainty materially weakens the Oral Presentation.

NOT_DEMONSTRATED.description: The student does not deliver the required Oral Presentation, is substantially unprepared, cannot explain essential evidence or model mechanics, gives materially inaccurate or invented responses, or does not demonstrate individual ownership.
